items.title: The Harness as the Only Mutable Surface: Compliance-Bounded Self-Evolution of LLM Agents in Credit Pipelines, with a Measured Admission Gate
items.one_liner: Confining self-evolving LLM agent modifications to runtime harnesses with a strict admission gate enables compliance-safe credit pipeline adaptation.
items.summary: Researchers propose a dual-loop engine for self-improving LLM agents in credit pipelines that confines adaptation strictly to the runtime harness while keeping model weights fixed. This boundary ensures every self-modification generates a reviewable diff, test, and hash-chained deployment record governed by an admission gate. In simulations across three supervisory re-interpretation severities, the gated loop admitted 144 out of 7,449 candidate changes without worsening held-out errors, whereas an unbounded system admitted 309 harmful changes. The gate successfully mapped to EU AI Act provisions for high-risk credit scoring while highlighting the exclusion of agentic AI from April 2026 US model-risk guidance.

items.bottom_line: Self-evolving LLM agents can safely adapt credit pipelines only when modifications are strictly confined to reviewable runtime harnesses governed by a cryptographic admission gate.

items.title: Curating Always-Loaded Context for LLM Agents: A Capacitated Assortment Model with Censored Feedback
items.one_liner: A formal model for LLM agent context curation shows that simply appending instructions degrades performance and complicates feedback-driven pruning.
items.summary: Context curation for LLM agents is formulated as a capacitated assortment problem under censored feedback, addressing how fixed context files degrade performance as they grow. Adding instructions consumes a finite attention capacity, and appending every instruction with positive standalone value can be significantly worse than selecting an optimal subset. Because missing instructions generate feedback only when their absence causes harm, deleting ignored rules can inadvertently remove helpful ones. Empirical experiments show that irrelevant rules drawn from real context files reduce language-model compliance.
items.bottom_line: Unchecked instruction appending in LLM agent context files reduces model compliance and requires principled assortment models to manage token budgets.

items.title: False Claims, Credible Images: A Red-Teaming Benchmark for Commercial Image Generators
items.one_liner: EpiReal-Bench and EpiReal-Attack highlight significant alignment vulnerabilities in commercial image generators that easily produce convincing visual misinformation.
items.summary: Commercial image generators easily produce credible visual misinformation, such as fake news reports and textbook pages, despite safeguards that evaluate general harmful content rather than false assertions. To address this gap, researchers introduced EpiReal-Bench, a systematic benchmark comprising 10k false-claim prompts and generated images across 10 real-world claim categories and visual formats. items.title: Attackers Target Rejetto HFS Flaw That Enables Admin Session Forgery and RCE
items.one_liner: Rejetto HFS CVE-2026-61500 is under active exploitation due to a weak Math.random() PRNG session signing implementation.
items.summary: Rejetto HTTP File Server versions 3.0.0 through 3.2.0 are under active exploitation for CVE-2026-61500, a critical session forgery vulnerability with a CVSS score of 9.3. The flaw stems from using the weak, non-cryptographic Math.random() PRNG in JavaScript to derive session-cookie signing keys, which are exposed to unauthenticated clients during login. Attackers can collect login responses to reconstruct the PRNG state, forge an administrator session cookie, and leverage the server_code configuration feature for remote code execution. A Python proof-of-concept was released in late September by Alejandro Ramos following Anthropic Mythos-assisted discovery, prompting scanning activity originating from China Telecom IPs.

items.title: UN extends Darfur arms embargo, blocks broader Sudan sanctions proposal
items.one_liner: The UN Security Council extended the Darfur arms embargo by two months while blocking a nationwide Sudan expansion proposal.
items.summary: The United Nations Security Council unanimously adopted Resolution 2830 to extend the arms embargo on Sudan's Darfur region by two months until December 11, 2026, alongside the monitoring panel's mandate until January 11, 2027. The short-term technical rollover follows a previous one-month renewal on September 11. Permanent members Russia and China opposed a broader US proposal to expand the arms embargo across the entire territory of Sudan, arguing that the existing 20-year-old framework is sufficient. The ongoing conflict between the Sudanese army and the Rapid Support Forces has caused massive casualties and displaced 13 million people.
items.bottom_line: Geopolitical division among UN Security Council members has blocked a nationwide arms embargo in Sudan, resulting in a short-term technical rollover for Darfur.

items.title: Zambia signs US health deal after disputes over data-sharing
items.one_liner: Zambia's new US health financing agreement resolves privacy concerns over medical data sharing after earlier leaked drafts sparked intense public pushback.
items.summary: Zambia has signed a five-year, $1.5bn health financing agreement with the US, resolving a public dispute over data-sharing and mineral rights. The revised text removes controversial clauses requiring biological specimen shipments to the US and restricts data exchanges to program monitoring, protecting individual patient privacy. The agreement replaces previous USAID-channelled funding to support HIV/AIDS, malaria, and maternal health as part of a shared responsibility model. Washington has pursued similar deals across Africa following the closure of USAID, while several other nations have rejected agreements over data terms.
items.bottom_line: Zambia's revised US health funding deal successfully preserves patient privacy by dropping controversial biological specimen and wide data-sharing mandates.
